figures.caption: Figure 1: Multimodal peripheral decoder architecture and performance. (A) Network architecture: each input modality (EEG, EDA, HR/HRV, RESP, Pupil) is independently embedded by a Conv1D+BatchNorm temporal encoder, embeddings are concatenated, and a two-layer MLP classifier produces the arousal index. (B) Within-subject AUC for the original FBCSP benchmark, a retrained EEG-only decoder, the autonomic-only decoder, and the combined autonomic+EEG decoder. Error bars are SEM across subjects. (C) Integrated Gradients feature attribution by modality across the 2-second pre-event epoch. Cardiac signals (HR) dominate; EDA contributes substantially; respiration shows a late-epoch rise.

Figure 2: Yerkes-Dodson validation. (A) Quadratic fit of trial-level performance versus mean decoded arousal for the multimodal peripheral decoder (“New”). Both linear and quadratic terms are significant (p < 0.01). Hard course shown in red, easy course in blue; shaded bands are 95% confidence intervals from the mixed-effects model; dashed vertical lines mark the estimated optima (∼ 51 for both courses). (B) Corresponding plot for the Faller et al EEG decoder (“Old”): curve is shallower, and the estimated optima diverge between easy (∼ 62) and hard (∼ 76) courses. (C) AIC comparison across model variants relative to the best model (the new quadratic).

Figure 3: Baseline physiology modulates individual arousal-performance curves. (A) Estimated arousal-performance curves as a function of baseline HRV (z-scored), derived from the mixed-effects model. High-HRV (blue, tolerant) subjects show a broad, near-monotonic relationship; low-HRV (red, sensitive) subjects show a sharply peaked curve with steep decline at high arousal. The arousal2 × HRV interaction is significant (p = 0.017). (B) Corresponding curves as a function of baseline gamma power. High-gamma (blue, sensitive) subjects show a steep, narrow peak; low-gamma (red, tolerant) subjects show a broader, flatter relationship. The arousal2 ×Gamma interaction is significant (p = 0.036).

Figure 4: Optimal arousal trajectory and performance prediction. (A) Heatmap of mean flight time as a joint function of decoded arousal (y-axis) and trial time (x-axis), computed from hard-course control trials; warmer colors indicate lower mean flight time. The blue dashed line is the polynomial-fit optimal trajectory derived from the row of peak performance at each time bin. (B) Trial-level scatter of flight time versus % time within the optimal band (r = 0.308, p < 0.001). (C) Mean arousal traces (± SEM) for top-quartile (green), middle (gray), and bottom-quartile (red) trials, overlaid on the optimal trajectory (black dashed) and ±1 SD confidence band (gray shading). Bad trials rise above the optimal trajectory early; good trials track it closely from below. (D) % time within optimal band by performance tertile. Good trials spend ∼ 80% in band, bad trials ∼ 57% (p < 0.01, Holm-corrected).

Figure 5: Deviation-performance coupling differs by arousal sensitivity. (A) Trial-level scatter of flight time versus % time within optimal band, separated by sensitivity group. Sensitive subjects (red, r = 0.39, p = 0.003) show a substantially stronger relationship than tolerant subjects (blue, r = 0.26, p = 0.045). (B) Restricting to the most extreme cases (5 most sensitive, 4 most tolerant) amplifies the difference: the sensitive subgroup retains a strong slope (r = 0.34) while the tolerant subgroup is essentially flat (r = 0.19, p = 0.336). A uniform threshold is therefore mismatched to one of the two groups.

Figure 6: Personalized threshold optimization. (A) Optimal arousal trajectory (black line) with the universal (×1 SD, gray), sensitive (×1.5 SD, red), and tolerant (×2.5 SD, blue) control bands. (B) Cohen’s d between good and bad trials on the % time above band metric as a function of band width multiplier for the arousal-sensitive group; selected ms = 1.5 peaks at d = 1.32 (compared to d = 1.21 at m = 1.0). (C) Same for the arousal-tolerant group; selected mt = 2.5 peaks at d = 1.10 (compared to d = 0.85 at m = 1.0). (D) Trial-level scatter of flight time versus % time within the universal ×1 SD band (r = 0.308). Trials are colored by performance tertile. (E) Same scatter under the personalized band (r = 0.359). The bottom-quartile (red) trials are more cleanly separated from the middle and top trials under the personalized policy.
